headline: SpaceX starts in-house turbine blade manufacturing to cut AI data center generator delays by 18 months
summary: SpaceX's new in-house turbine blade production aims to bypass long grid connection wait times and existing engine shortages, significantly accelerating the deployment of AI data centers.
details: The U.S. electricity supply is a major bottleneck for new AI data centers. Many projects are turning to portable natural gas turbine generators to bypass long grid connection wait times. To address this, Elon Musk announced SpaceX will bring turbine blade and vane casting in-house.

Musk was an early adopter of these 'portable' generators for his Colossus data center in Memphis, bringing it online rapidly. OpenAI has also announced plans to deploy turbines at its Stargate data center for additional power.

This sudden surge in demand from AI data centers has led to jet engine shortages. Engine manufacturers were unprepared for the AI boom, and commercial aviation already faced its own supply chain issues.

Manufacturing turbine blades and vanes is a significant bottleneck, with production often taking 60 to 90 weeks per batch. These specialized parts require extreme precision due to the forces and temperatures they withstand.

By bringing this production in-house, Musk believes SpaceX can cut generator delivery times by 18 months. This would allow xAI to acquire new turbine generators much faster, avoiding queues that could stretch into 2030.

While SpaceX and Tesla are rapidly building solar capacity, Musk states natural gas will be essential to supplement solar for several years. This investment in turbine manufacturing reflects the ongoing demand for data center power.

Musk has reportedly also acquired a billion-dollar fleet of portable gas and diesel turbines. While the exact manufacturing methods for these complex blades are unclear, Musk has a history of tackling challenging engineering problems.

headline_marked: [[Claude Code automatically appends session URLs]] to commit messages and PR descriptions by default
headline: Claude Code automatically appends session URLs to commit messages and PR descriptions by default
summary: Every commit message and PR description created by Claude Code automatically includes a session URL at the bottom. Users discover it only after it's already polluting their git history, with no opt-in or warning.
details: Every commit message and PR description generated by Claude Code automatically includes a session URL (e.g., https://claude.ai/code/session_...). This occurs without any opt-in prompt, warning, or mention during the onboarding process for users.

Developers are discovering these URLs only after they have already been added to their git history, leading to an unprofessional appearance and clutter in commit logs. Teammates and open-source contributors also see these unexpected links.

Users suggest making the session URL attribution an opt-in feature, perhaps with a one-time prompt during onboarding. Alternatives include a discoverable opt-out setting during the first commit or removing the feature entirely, relying on existing Co-Authored-By: Claude trailers.
